Reed man Buddy Collette is one of the most recognized jazz figures on the West Coast. He was born in Los Angeles on August 6, 1921 and grew up in the fertile music atmosphere of Central Avenue. Buddy was a mentor for Eric Dolphy and Charles Mingus and has played an important role as an educator throughout his career. He was part of the Stars of Swing in 1946 and later gained recognition with the Chico Hamilton Quintet in 1951. Buddy was the first black musician to be hired in the Los Angeles studios and was instrumental in the merging of the two separate musician’s locals. He is recognized as one of the great jazz flutists and has recorded prolifically since the 1950s.
Buddy was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 13, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Los Angeles, and I feel very privileged to have Buddy Collette with me.
Well Monk it’s my pleasure to be invited to be a part of this, you know I was happy when you gave me a call and then you sent the letter and I’m saying boy I could hardly wait for this to happen.
